tests.name: energy_collapse
tests.underflow_note: No underflow in the first 30 primes: smallest E_p = 2.738e-22 at p=113; double underflows (E->0) only near p~1548 (phi^-p < 5e-324). 0 of 30 values underflowed to exactly 0.

tests.name: phi_euler_product
tests.reason: Every factor (1 - phi^(-p s))^(-1) is finite and nonzero for Re(s)>0 since |phi^(-p s)| = phi^(-p/2) < 1, so the finite product Z is bounded away from 0 and has no zeros.

verdict: The draft's phi-decay model fails its own test: fitting g_n = A*phi^(-c*n) to GROWING prime gaps forces the exponent negative (c=-5.83572e-05 at N=10000), i.e. the 'decay' law must run backwards, and even then the log-linear R2 is only 0.0109934 (fixed-c=1 R2=-3228460.0, effectively no fit). The PNT logarithmic model g_n ~ b*log(p_n) is the honest description (b=1.0029, R2=0.0186119 at N=10000), and the energy claim E_p=p*phi^(-p) has essentially no correlation with actual gaps (r=-0.3388). The phi-Euler product has min |Z(1/2+it)|=0.490569 over t in [0,50], never zero, so QPGL's central phi-scaling mechanism is refuted on its own terms: the logarithmic model wins, and the golden-ratio scaling carries no predictive content for prime gaps.
